name: Authentication
purpose: Provide authentication-domain testing considerations that can be applied only when the supplied requirements contain corresponding authentication behavior.

coverage_dimensions.name: Credential Authentication
apply_when: The requirement describes authentication using credentials.

coverage_dimensions.name: Email Authentication
apply_when: The requirement explicitly uses email as an authentication identifier.

coverage_dimensions.name: Password Authentication
apply_when: The requirement explicitly uses a password for authentication.
consider: Password constraints explicitly stated in the requirement

coverage_dimensions.name: Case Sensitivity
apply_when: The requirement explicitly states that email or password comparison is case-sensitive or case-insensitive.

coverage_dimensions.name: Whitespace
apply_when: The requirement explicitly states trimming, preservation, rejection, or normalization of whitespace.
consider: Whitespace within the value when relevant

coverage_dimensions.name: Remember Me
apply_when: The requirement explicitly describes a Remember Me or persistent-login feature.

coverage_dimensions.name: Session Management
apply_when: The requirement explicitly describes sessions or authenticated-session behavior.

coverage_dimensions.name: SSO
apply_when: The requirement explicitly mentions SSO, OAuth, an identity provider, or an external authentication provider.

coverage_dimensions.name: Authorization
apply_when: The requirement explicitly describes roles, permissions, protected resources, or access restrictions.

coverage_dimensions.name: Authentication Security
apply_when: The requirement explicitly describes security controls or security-sensitive authentication behavior.

coverage_dimensions.name: Authentication Failure
apply_when: The requirement defines behavior when authentication fails.

traceability.rule: Every authentication test case must reference the requirement statement, rule, acceptance criterion, or explicitly described behavior that caused the scenario to be generated.

unknown_information.rule: If an authentication behavior is relevant but the requirement does not specify the expected result or policy, report the gap and use 'Requires QA Input' where necessary.

example.requirement: Users can log in using email and password.
